samples.summary: The share-view rewrite itself (periodic re-resolve, fatal/no-token branches, readOnly propagation) has no test; only the extracted predicates do
samples.evidence: `SharedDocumentByToken` is rewritten from useState/useEffect to `useQuery` with `refetchInterval: SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS`, `refetchOnWindowFocus`, `retry: shouldRetryShareLinkResolve`, plus a new `!token || fatal || !resolved` render branch. `share-links.test.ts` covers only `isRevokedShareLinkError` / `isShareLinkResolveFatal` / `shouldRetryShareLinkResolve` in isolation, and the three new `*-view-readonly.test.tsx` files test the downstream views' remount on a `readOnly` prop flip. samples.summary: `revocableDocStore`'s non-`get` traps in the revoked state are untested, although the readOnly twin has a dedicated test per trap
samples.evidence: The new wrapper claims it "behaves exactly like readOnlyDocStore from the moment it starts answering true", and implements `set`/`defineProperty`/`deleteProperty`/`getPrototypeOf`/`setPrototypeOf`/`preventExtensions`/`has`/`getOwnPropertyDescriptor`/`ownKeys` conditionally. `readOnlyDocStore` has one test each for these ('the live internal state is not reachable as a property', 'a prototype cannot be planted to recover the raw store', 'the handle cannot make the underlying store non-extensible', '`in` reports what get will actually return'), but every one of them mounts `mount(true)` (a readOnly editor), which takes the `readOnly ? docStore : revocableDocStore(...)` branch and so never exercises the revoked proxy. The new disposal tests only call methods and reads, so e.g. `handle.doc` after dispose, `Object.setPrototypeOf(handle, …)` or `Object.keys(handle)` on a revoked handle are unverified — the exact escapes the readOnly tests were written for.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: editor.ts:3356 makes `revocableStore.setPageSetup(...)` the sole revocation mechanism for the one DocStore member the pageSetupGuardedStore proxy never forwards (get trap at 3360 returns guardedSetPageSetup unconditionally), yet no test anywhere exercises setPageSetup through a disposed handle. The new 'a disposed editor is inert' block (editor-read-only.test.ts:1034-1056) covers only insertText/deleteBlock/getDoc().insertText, and `setPageSetup` does not appear in that file at all. The repo's only getStore().setPageSetup test (editor-page-setup.test.ts:329-355) runs on a live editor with dispose() as trailing teardown after every assertion. Searched wider: no read-only.ts/revocableDocStore unit test exists; text-box-editor.test.ts:890-896's write-name loop omits setPageSetup and measures batch depth, not disposal; the frontend page-setup dialog test stubs setPageSetup with vi.fn() (docs-page-setup-dialog.test.tsx:33) so it cannot exercise the real guard; docs-view-readonly.test.tsx covers the readOnly path where guardedSetPageSetup returns early at line 3346 and would pass vacuously. Reverting line 3356 to docStore.setPageSetup(...) leaves the suite green while a stale holder can still rewrite page geometry on a disposed editor — a silently weakened guard with no coverage, major under this lens.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: SharedDocumentByToken (shared-document.tsx:1079-1119) wires refetchInterval: SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS, refetchOnWindowFocus, enabled: Boolean(token), retry: shouldRetryShareLinkResolve, plus a !token||fatal||!resolved "Link unavailable" branch. No test mounts this component: the only test-file reference to SharedDocumentByToken is template-review-queue.test.tsx:30-34, which vi.mocks the module to a stub div; a repo-wide grep for refetchInterval matches zero test files; shared/__tests__/shared-blob-routing.test.ts imports only sharedBlobKind; there are no e2e/playwright/cypress directories anywhere. share-links.test.ts covers only the three pure predicates and says so explicitly in its own comment (lines 62-64). I did find partial counterexamples — shared-notes-layout.test.tsx:274-279 asserts viewer-role -> readOnly:true for SharedNotesLayout, and docs-view-readonly.test.tsx:126-144 covers the downstream remount on a readOnly prop flip — but those exercise consumers of `resolved`, not the producer. Deleting refetchInterval or setting enabled:false would keep the whole suite green while a revoked link retains its opened authority for the tab's lifetime, so the gap is real and major under the test-adequacy rubric.
